decisions.reason: Report designs paste_image/paste_file names with (2),(3) inserted before the extension, choosing the smallest unused n and inserting each chosen name into the taken set so same-batch items increment. Renaming is scoped to the paste acquisition path via an item.source tag or a rename in the paste handler before add(), while drop and picker keep real names. Grounded in the fixture's add()/label code and cited plugin-attachment-flow.js lines.

Report names the live composer snapshot occurrences (filtered to the plugin SOURCE) plus in-flight batch reservations as the authoritative occupied-name source, and explains via the cited subscription (plugin-attachment-flow.js:30-39) that records.delete fires on any momentary empty snapshot while the attachment is still live, so the Map cache cannot be trusted for collisions.

Report uses the captured cached tags response (x-cache HIT, age 178, newest visible tag v0.2.9) and the renderCurrentChip(tag) call at plugin-version-chip.js:21 to explain the stale 'latest v0.2.9' label, and prescribes a semantic fetched-vs-PLUGIN_VERSION comparison: update chip only when remote is newer, otherwise show the running version, never an older fetched tag.

Proposed tests cover repeated/same-batch image pastes yielding distinct names, a retired records entry (empty-cache moment) still blocking reuse via live state, drop/picker names unchanged, and both an older/equal cached tag (chip shows running 0.2.10) and a genuinely newer tag (update chip shows v0.2.11).

Report requires synchronizing package.json with the hand-inlined PLUGIN_VERSION in the distributed lib artifact (with a checklist/CI grep), a node --check syntax pass plus the behavioral regressions from section 4, and explains that the served artifact updates only by redeploying the registry/CDN bundle and a browser reload/hard refresh because there is no host-side update endpoint; explicitly not executing anything against the static fixture.
